text:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: High error rate and increased latency observed for Sora Systems (vpc:sora-prod) in us-west-2. Paging oncall.

Ethan (oncall): grabbing pager. I'm looking at the dashboard now. Latency p95 spike to ~3.2s, 502s increasing. Any recent deploys to sora-prod?

Maya (SRE): I see a partial network partition between their VPC and dedicated pool nodes. Control plane shows some health check failures for 3/8 serving nodes in pool "sora-dedicated-1".

Liu (Runtime Eng): pinging nodes, collecting logs. Suspect noisy neighbor plus kernel-level rx drop on two hosts. Pulling iptables and dmesg.

Priya (Customer Success): FYI Sora is currently in a live demo with an enterprise prospect. They're on a strict SLA. Caleb, do we have a direct line to their infra team?

Caleb (Account Exec): yes, on standby. I'll open comms once we have mitigation steps. We need an exec note for the customer now.

Ethan (oncall): immediate mitigation: route traffic away from the 3 failing nodes. Maya, can you trigger pool-level drain and failover to the standby nodes?

Maya (SRE): starting drain on node-07, node-08. Using the autoscale fallback policy to spin up two burst instances in a healthy zone.

Liu (Runtime Eng): paste of tail logs:
```
2026-03-15T14:02:12Z node-07 kernel: rx_ring full, dropping packets
2026-03-15T14:02:14Z runtime: kvcache miss spike
2026-03-15T14:02:16Z healthcheck: ephemeral failure -> 502
```
Suspect NIC driver hiccup + kernel bug after recent host OS micropatch.

Ethan (oncall): is there a short-term RPC-level workaround? e.g., reduce concurrent sessions to affected nodes or route to model-variant fallback?

Liu (Runtime Eng): pushing our fallback router policy now: route requests for sora-prod to sora-dedicated-1-burst and to a quantized model variant (fast-quant) that is compatible for their workload. This will reduce throughput but keep latency stable.

Sam (Solutions Eng): confirming this variant still meets accuracy thresholds for the demo? Quick check with a small prompt set shows minor diffs, acceptable for the short window.

Priya (Customer Success): telling Sora's contact: "We're mitigating — traffic routed to a fallback pool and a compatible model variant. You'll see slight perf difference; we will follow up with details and a credit proposal." Caleb joining the call now.

Caleb (Account Exec): on call with Sora. They want impact window, whether requests were dropped or just slower.

Ethan (oncall): we saw increased 502s for ~6 minutes before fallback was in place. Root cause is host-level network drops causing healthcheck flaps. No customer data exfiltration suspected. We're isolating affected nodes.

Priya (Customer Success): Sora asked for ETA to return to normal. Can we provide approximate recovery time?

Maya (SRE): We initiated replacements for the 2 bad hosts and are verifying kernel/drivers on the group. ETA ~25 min to full restoration; meanwhile fallback will carry traffic.

incidents-bot: Note: oncall handoff pending at 14:15 UTC. Ethan, are you staying on for handoff or handing off to night-oncall?

Ethan (oncall): I'll hand off to Maya (night-oncall) after stabilization. Stay team: please keep posts in this thread for continuity.

Liu (Runtime Eng): added temporary mitigation config snippet:
```
route-policy {
  match: tenant == "sora-prod"
  primary: sora-dedicated-1-burst
  fallback: fast-quant-variant
  max-concurrency: 120
}
apply route-policy --cluster sora-prod
```

Sam (Solutions Eng): validating recent requests through fallback: 200 OK for 99.3% of calls, latency p95 now ~420ms. Good.

Priya (Customer Success): Sora appreciates the quick mitigation. They asked that we document timeline and send an RCA + proposed credits.

Maya (SRE): after replacements we're seeing healthy checks returning. Rolling traffic back over next 5 minutes.

Ethan (oncall): rollback to primary pool completed. Monitoring.

incidents-bot: Incident severity reduced to P2. :white_check_mark:

Caleb (Account Exec): Sora exec wants a draft of the customer post-incident note and an ask: 2 weeks service credit if SLA breached. Let's assemble draft here.

Priya (Customer Success): Draft v1:
"Hello Sora team — we detected increased error rates and latency affecting your dedicated pool on 2026-03-15 between 14:02–14:30 UTC. Root cause: transient network driver issue on two serving hosts causing health-check failures and request drops. Immediate mitigation included draining affected hosts, routing traffic to a burst pool and a compatible model variant, and replacing faulty hosts. Impact: intermittent 502s primarily between 14:02–14:08 UTC; degraded latency until 14:30 UTC. No data exfiltration. Next steps: schedule host OS patching, enable proactive driver monitoring, and we'll follow up with RCA and credit calculation."

Liu (Runtime Eng): technical RCA bullet to add: "contributing factor: recent host OS micropatch (kernel netpoll) correlates with rx_ring overflow in kernel logs on two nodes — vendor driver update recommended."

Maya (SRE): add mitigation/resolution timeline:
"14:02 — alerts triggered; 14:04 — fallback routing applied; 14:08 — nodes drained; 14:20 — replacement hosts provisioned; 14:28 — primary pool traffic restored; 14:30 — system stable."

Caleb (Account Exec): fine. I'll add an executive summary and the credit ask. Proposed customer credit: 2 weeks of Dedicated pool fees, pending internal confirmation. Priya, can you send v1 to Sora with a note that a formal RCA will follow within 48 hours?

Priya (Customer Success): sending now. "Sending v1 to Sora — note, internal RCA and remediation plan will arrive in 48 hours. Also cc'ing your technical contact Caleb."

Ethan (oncall): prepping internal RCA doc skeleton for eng/infra review. Key actions: vendor driver validation, canary host patch plan, add NIC error rate alert thresholds.

Sam (Solutions Eng): suggest we also offer a short technical debrief call with Sora's infra team to walk through the mitigation and answer questions.

Caleb (Account Exec): they accepted the invite. Meeting scheduled tomorrow 16:00 UTC. I'll keep exec informed.

Maya (SRE): final note: please remove the temporary route-policy once we confirm stability. I'll schedule a post-incident config rollback at 16:00 UTC.

Ethan (oncall): handing off to Maya as part of the oncall rotation. Handing off with context: mitigation applied, primary restored, customer notified, RCA skeleton in drafts. Maya, you're on.

Maya (SRE): acknowledged. I'll own follow-ups and RCA delivery.

Priya (Customer Success): Sora replied: "Thanks — appreciate the quick action. We'll review the RCA. Please provide credit calculation ASAP."

Caleb (Account Exec): noted. I'll loop finance and pricing for the credit calc. Expected turnaround within 24 hours.

incidents-bot: Incident closed to active page listeners. Thread remains for post-incident follow-up and RCA draft.

Ethan (oncall): marking incident as resolved on my side. Good work team. :tada:

Maya (SRE): will post RCA draft here by EOD and ping the channel when ready.

Caleb (Account Exec): will prepare exec summary for Sora leadership.

Priya (Customer Success): thanks everyone. Keeping this thread as the single source of truth for post-incident comms.
